Vendor advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-p3gq-pcg9-qvfv is state=published, withdrawn_at=null. It quotes public_key_part() returning private_key[:16] and the silent `if shared_secret is None: shared_secret = simulation_secret` assignment.

findings: Real, non-withdrawn vulnerability: silent KEM-decapsulation fallback in openssl_encrypt/modules/pqc.py substitutes SHA-256(public encapsulated_key || first 16 private-key bytes) as the AEAD key. CVE-2026-74900 is PUBLISHED; vendor GHSA-p3gq-pcg9-qvfv is published.
Atomic BIC is 5e3104481d9842d3d6989332ae32bee4b010d2db versus parent 295bf5f3df60ce08d2d8aed26d4fa0bc03592850, which still used kem.decapsulate with no simulation substitute.
Direct fix is 472c088be14f5edb3dde1bf819419a8b86c8d72f; present in v1.4.0 and absent from v1.3.6. Affected membership is v1.0.0 through v1.3.6 inclusive, matching CVE <1.4.0.
BIC commit message itself records Claude Code generation and Claude co-authorship, so AI authored the root-cause fallback. Primary verdict AI_ROOT_CAUSE stands.

Advisory wording that 16 leaked private-key bytes decrypt 'all ciphertext' overstates the successful-KEM path; the code still uses the real shared secret when decap succeeds. That imprecision is already in the primary bug_semantics caveat and does not change the CWE-391 finding or the verdict.
